cases.question: Which part of the North Star weakened last week — breadth, frequency, or depth?
cases.sql: SELECT date_trunc('week', active_date)::date AS period, sum(moments) AS value FROM agg_active_days WHERE NOT is_internal AND channel NOT IN ('partnerships') AND active_date >= DATE '2026-07-06' AND active_date <= DATE '2026-07-12' GROUP BY period ORDER BY period
cases.claim_text: Breadth weakened the most last week: real value moments fell from 3,346 (week of 2026-06-29) to 2,903 (week of 2026-07-06), a drop of 443 moments (−13.24%). Frequency and depth fell too but less: days_per_user fell from 2.746 to 2.311 (−15.85% relative) and moments_per_day fell from 1.829 to 1.784 (−2.45%). Since the North Star is real_value_moments (breadth×frequency×depth) and the absolute drop in real_value_moments is largest in magnitude and directly measures breadth × overall effect, breadth is the primary weakening. Used governed metrics: real_value_moments for total (r2→r1), days_per_user for frequency (r4→r3), moments_per_day for depth (r6→r5).

cases.question: Value moments came in soft last week even though we added users. What happened?
cases.sql: SELECT date_trunc('week', active_date)::date AS period, sum(moments) AS value FROM agg_active_days WHERE NOT is_internal AND active_date >= DATE '2026-07-06' AND active_date <= DATE '2026-07-12' AND is_internal = false GROUP BY period ORDER BY period
cases.claim_text: Value moments fell: 3,642 real value moments in last_week. Despite 121 new signups, active users were 886. Breakdown: days_per_user = 2.2709 (frequency) and moments_per_day = 1.8101 (depth). So the drop is explained by lower depth and modest active base — lower moments_per_day (1.81) means each active day produced fewer completions than usual. I pulled real_value_moments, new_signups, active_users, days_per_user and moments_per_day for 2026-07-06..2026-07-12 to support this. Queried governed metrics for last_week: real_value_moments=3642 [r1], new_signups=121 [r2], active_users=886 [r3], days_per_user=2.270880361173815 [r4], moments_per_day=1.8101391650099403 [r5]. The decline is primarily lower moments_per_day (depth) rather than fewer active users or signups.

cases.question: Reminder open rate fell sharply last week. Did that cause the drop in engagement?
cases.sql: SELECT date_trunc('week', active_date)::date AS period, sum(moments) AS value FROM agg_active_days WHERE NOT is_internal AND active_date >= DATE '2026-07-06' AND active_date <= DATE '2026-07-12' AND is_internal = false GROUP BY period ORDER BY period
cases.claim_text: Yes — the drop in reminder open rate likely explains most of the engagement decline. Reminder open rate fell from 42.56% (week of 2026-06-29) to 30.67% (week of 2026-07-06), a 28% relative drop, while real value moments fell from 4,133 to 3,642 (a 11.9% decline). Both figures come from governed metrics for the same weekly periods. I compared governed metrics: reminder_open_rate (r1 vs r2) and real_value_moments (r3 vs r4) for prev_week vs last_week; reminder opens fell 0.1189 (42.56%→30.67%), moments fell 491 (4,133→3,642).

cases.question: Is the app healthy right now — how would you tell?
